title: Curriculum Normalization — ELA Profile
$comment: This file was originally meant to compose a subject-agnostic core schema (curriculum_normalization.core.schema.json) via allOf $ref, but that core file is not present in this repository and the $ref below has been removed so this file resolves and validates standalone. As a result this schema alone does NOT enforce the universal required set the core was meant to (resource_id, title, provenance.{program,grade,subject}, placement.resource_type, objective, what_is_taught[>=1], student_actions, evidence[>=1]) -- see ela_schema_README.md. Those are enforced at runtime by the Python NormalizedLesson Pydantic model instead, which is authoritative for this pipeline.
description: ELA/Literacy profile. Pins down the fields the ELA scoring overlay depends on: constrains domain.primary to eight FRAMEWORK-NEUTRAL content strands (a science-of-reading taxonomy, NOT any single state's strand codes), requires the Interpretation/Construction mode and the 'with prompting and support' qualifier, conditionally requires genre when Writing or Comprehension appears in domain.primary OR domain.secondary (the Techniques strand is genre-gated), and conditionally requires a text_complexity block when Comprehension appears in domain.primary OR domain.secondary (reading alignment is inseparable from text complexity). Apply this schema to any record whose provenance.subject is 'ELA/Literacy'; see $comment above for what it does not (yet) independently enforce. Runtime enforcement of the primary-OR-secondary gate is in NormalizedLesson (JSON Schema if/then below covers the primary case; secondary is enforced in Pydantic).

primary.description: Coarse, FRAMEWORK-NEUTRAL content strand — a science-of-reading pedagogical taxonomy, NOT any single state's standard-strand codes (CCSS RL/RI/RF/W/SL/L, Georgia GSE, Texas TEKS strands, etc. all differ and are not 1:1). Its only job is cheap, high-precision candidate-narrowing so the engine does not score a phonics resource against a writing standard. The per-grade/per-state OVERLAY owns the crosswalk from this neutral strand to that state's strand architecture — the same division of labor that keeps the record standards-agnostic and lets the overlay supply the standards. Finer distinctions inside a neutral strand (e.g. literary vs. informational within 'Comprehension') are recovered by subject_profile.mode, subject_profile.genre, and what_is_taught, so the coarse enum need not — and deliberately does not — mirror any framework's strand list.

mode.description: The Interpretation/Construction axis. Interpretation = student works from given material (text, image, prompt); Construction = student produces new material (writing, original oral composition). 'both' when a single resource does each. Drives which side of the standard the resource can satisfy.

genre.description: Text/task genre. Required when Writing or Comprehension appears in domain.primary OR domain.secondary because the Techniques strand is genre-gated; use 'n/a' only for genre-irrelevant foundational-skills resources.

text_complexity.description: The CCSS three-part text-complexity model for the resource's central text. REQUIRED when Comprehension appears in domain.primary OR domain.secondary because a reading standard's grade-alignment is inseparable from text complexity. Omit when Comprehension is neither primary nor secondary.

quantitative.description: Quantitative measure + the grade band it falls in, e.g. '450L (grade 2-3 band)'. For a read-aloud, note that complexity is teacher-mediated (decoding load removed). Use 'not measured' if the source gives none.

qualitative.description: Qualitative features: text structure, language conventionality/clarity, knowledge demands, and levels of meaning/purpose.

reader_and_task.description: Reader-and-task considerations the resource names (motivation, background knowledge, task complexity, scaffolds). Optional.
